item.title: Updates from the UN General Assembly 2026
item.description: Marking the opening of the 81st UN General Assembly, Crisis Group experts discuss challenges facing the UN’s efforts to promote international peace and security. This page includes updates from the High-Level Week in New York and recent Crisis Group coverage of the UN.
item.dc:creator: eschelhaas

item.title: Les pays africains face à la crise de l’ONU
item.description: Dans cet épisode d’Afrique 360°, Enrica Picco et Rinaldo Depagne reçoivent Karim Soumana, directeur du Projet Ordre Global et Maintien de la Paix de Crisis Group et ancien ambassadeur du Niger aux Nations unies, pour examiner la crise du multilatéralisme du point de vue de l’Afrique et les perspectives d’un renforcement des voix africaines au sein des institutions multilatérales, dont la première d’entre elles, l’ONU.
item.dc:creator: mloukili

item.title: Somalia Awaits a New Security Order as Mission Drawdown Looms
item.description: The multilateral missions that have helped the Somali government fight Al-Shabaab for nearly two decades may be coming to an end. Mogadishu and its partners should get started now developing a plan for what they will do next.
item.dc:creator: pfranz

item.title: The UN’s High Level Week, Secretary-General Selection and “Middle Power” Problem
item.description: This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard Atwood is joined by Crisis Group experts Richard Gowan and Daniel Forti to discuss next week’s UN General Assembly high-level week and whether a new Secretary-General can revive the organisation’s peacemaking as global turmoil spreads.
item.dc:creator: hschaub

item.title: The Houthis, the Saudis and the New Red Sea Politics
item.description: This week on The Horn, Alan talks with Crisis Group experts Yasmine Farouk and Ahmed Nagi about what’s behind the Houthi offensive in Yemen, Saudi Arabia’s response and the implications of emerging Saudi-backed security partnerships for the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa.
item.dc:creator: hschaub

item.title: Closing the New War Front in Yemen
item.description: The Houthis’ rapid advance on the western Yemeni coast has opened a new front in the Middle East war that began with February’s U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran. A truce in Yemen is an urgent priority, so that hostilities do not spiral, drawing in more countries.
item.dc:creator: cthuratong

item.title: On Our Radar
item.description: On Our Radar scans conflicts and crises around the globe every week and features some of the hotspots Crisis Group’s analysts are closely watching. Whether an under-reported trend or a headline-grabbing development, our field experts explain why it matters or what should be done.
item.dc:creator: eschelhaas

item.title: A Pivotal Moment in Uniting Post-Assad Syria
item.description: The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, which long enjoyed de facto autonomy in north-eastern Syria, have dissolved. But tensions in the region remain high as talks about integration with the central state proceed. Further compromise would set a useful precedent for other parts of the country.
item.dc:creator: eschelhaas

item.title: Special Episode: Will the Houthis Shut Down the Bab al-Mandab Strait?
item.description: In this special episode of Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group expert Ahmed Nagi about the rapid Houthi advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, what they mean for Saudi Arabia and the wider region, and the risk of a broader shipping crisis.
